items.question: What is the maximum total number of occupants, including crew, in high-density configuration?
items.explanation: In high-density cabin configuration the total number of occupants, including crew, shall not exceed 17.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: What is the maximum total number of occupants, including crew, in low-density configuration?
items.explanation: In low-density cabin configuration the total number of occupants, including crew, shall not exceed 14.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: What is the minimum number of passenger seats that must remain installed in the cabin?
options: 3 seats in at least one row
items.explanation: The RFM requires that a minimum of 3 seats in at least one row remain installed in the cabin.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: NUMBER OF OCCUPANTS (p.1-1)

items.question: Under day VFR according to the basic RFM, what is the minimum flight crew requirement?
options: One pilot, single-pilot operation not permitted from left seat
Two pilots, one in each front seat
One pilot from either left or right seat
One pilot plus one flight engineer
items.explanation: For day VFR the minimum flight crew is one pilot, and single-pilot operation is not permitted from the left seat.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: MINIMUM FLIGHT CREW (p.1-1)

items.question: What is the maximum gross weight for towing or taxi?
items.explanation: Maximum gross weight for towing or taxi is 6450 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: What is the maximum gross weight for CAT B take-off and landing?
items.explanation: Maximum gross weight for Category B take-off and landing is 6400 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: What is the minimum flight/rotor running gross weight?
items.explanation: Minimum flight/rotor running gross weight is 4400 kg.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WEIGHT AND CENTER OF GRAVITY LIMITATIONS (p.1-2)

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed when operating with Take-Off Power?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed with Take-Off Power applied is 90 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed when main rotor speed NR is at 102%?
items.explanation: With NR at 102% the maximum airspeed is limited to 90 KIAS.

items.question: Minimum airspeed for flight under IFR (Vmini) is?
items.explanation: Vmini for IFR operations is 50 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for IFR approach?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for IFR approach is 150 KIAS.

items.question: Maximum airspeed for climb with one autopilot (AP) failed is?
items.explanation: With one AP failed the maximum airspeed for climb is 100 KIAS.

items.question: Maximum rate of climb with one autopilot (AP) failed is?
items.explanation: With one AP failed, the maximum permitted rate of climb is 1000 fpm.

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed with one autopilot (AP) failed?
items.explanation: With one AP failed the maximum airspeed is limited to Vne - 27 KIAS.

items.question: What is the maximum airspeed for landing gear operation and with landing gear extended (Vlo/Vle)?
items.explanation: Both maximum landing gear operating speed (Vlo) and gear extended speed (Vle) are 150 KIAS or Vne if less.

items.question: Minimum airspeed in autorotation is?
items.explanation: The minimum airspeed in autorotation is 40 KIAS.

items.question: Maximum airspeed with the right cabin door locked open is?
items.explanation: With the right cabin door locked open maximum airspeed is 100 KIAS.

items.question: Maximum airspeed with the left or both cabin doors locked open is?
items.explanation: With the left or both cabin doors locked open maximum airspeed is 80 KIAS.

items.question: Maximum airspeed for opening or closing the cabin doors is?
items.explanation: Opening or closing the cabin doors is limited to 80 KIAS.

items.question: Maximum airspeed for operation of the windscreen wipers is?
items.explanation: Maximum airspeed for operation of windscreen wipers is 140 KIAS.

items.question: On paved surfaces, what is the maximum taxi speed?
items.explanation: Maximum taxi speed on paved surfaces is 40 knots (74 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: On paved surfaces, what is the maximum speed for emergency landing (nose wheel locked fore and aft)?
items.explanation: Maximum speed for emergency landing on paved surfaces is 60 knots (110 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: What is the maximum towing speed on paved surfaces?
items.explanation: Maximum towing speed on paved surfaces is 37 km/hr (23 mph).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: On prepared grass surfaces, what is the maximum taxi speed?
items.explanation: On prepared grass, maximum taxi speed is 20 knots (37 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: On prepared grass surfaces, what is the maximum speed for emergency landing?
items.explanation: On prepared grass, maximum speed for emergency landing is 40 knots (74 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: GROUND SPEED LIMITATIONS (p.1-8)

items.question: What is the maximum wind speed for rotor starting and stopping?
items.explanation: Maximum wind speed for rotor starting and stopping is 60 knots (30 m/s).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WIND SPEED LIMITATIONS FOR ROTOR STARTING AND STOPPING (p.1-8)

items.question: When rotor starting/stopping with winds above 33 knots (17 m/s), what must be recorded?
options: Actual windspeed in the helicopter log book
items.explanation: For rotor starting and stopping with windspeeds above 33 knots, the actual windspeed must be recorded in the helicopter log book.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WIND SPEED LIMITATIONS FOR ROTOR STARTING AND STOPPING (p.1-8)

items.question: What is the minimum outside air temperature (OAT) for ground starting?
items.explanation: Minimum ambient air temperature for ground starting is -40 deg C.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: AMBIENT AIR TEMPERATURE LIMITATIONS (OAT)

items.question: According to the basic RFM, is flight into known icing conditions permitted?
options: Only with ice protection systems ON
items.explanation: The basic AW139 RFM states that flight into known icing conditions is prohibited.

items.question: According to the basic RFM, is flight into freezing rain permitted?
options: No, flight into freezing rain is prohibited
items.explanation: The basic RFM explicitly prohibits flight into freezing rain.

items.question: Are aerobatic manoeuvres permitted?
items.explanation: Section 1 MANOEUVRING LIMITATIONS states that aerobatic manoeuvres are prohibited.

items.question: Are practice autorotative landings permitted?
options: Yes, but only on paved surfaces
No, practice autorotative landings are prohibited
items.explanation: AUTOROTATION LIMITATIONS state that practice autorotative landings are prohibited.

items.question: During autorotation, when may the ENG MODE select switch be retarded from FLIGHT to IDLE?
options: Only when both engines are failed
items.explanation: The RFM states that during autorotation the ENG MODE select switch must not be retarded from FLIGHT to IDLE except in an emergency.

items.question: What are the basic RFM slope limitations for sloped take-off and landing?
items.explanation: In the basic RFM, sloped take-off and landing are limited to 5 deg nose up, 5 deg nose down, 5 deg left wing low and 5 deg right wing low.

items.question: What is the maximum running speed for wheel brake application?
items.explanation: Wheel brake limitations specify a maximum running speed for brake application of 40 knots (74 km/hr).
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WHEEL BRAKE LIMITATIONS (p.1-32)

items.question: How long is parking on slopes up to 10 deg permitted?
items.explanation: Parking on slopes up to 10 deg is permitted for a maximum of 1 hour.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: WHEEL BRAKE LIMITATIONS (p.1-32)

items.question: At what indicated OAT must pitot heating be switched ON?
items.explanation: Pitot heating must be switched ON for indicated outside air temperature of +4 deg C or less.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: PITOT HEATING LIMITATIONS (p.1-32)

items.question: At what indicated OAT must pitot heating be switched OFF?
items.explanation: Pitot heating must be switched OFF at indicated outside air temperature of +10 deg C or more.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: PITOT HEATING LIMITATIONS (p.1-32)

items.question: What is the total usable fuel capacity?
items.explanation: Total usable fuel capacity is 1588 litres.

items.question: What is the unusable fuel quantity?
items.explanation: Unusable fuel quantity is 20 litres.

items.question: In coordinated flight, what unusable fuel is indicated and what is the actual per tank?
options: 0 kg indicated / 5 kg per tank actual
0 kg indicated / 8 kg (10 litres) per tank actual
5 kg indicated / 8 kg per tank actual
8 kg indicated / 10 kg per tank actual
items.explanation: In coordinated flight the indication is 0 kg unusable, which corresponds to 8 kg/10 litres per tank actual.

items.question: When is hovering in crosswinds or sideways flight with sustained roll angles greater than 15 deg prohibited?
options: When either tank indicates less than 50 kg
When either tank indicates less than 60 kg
When either tank indicates less than 70 kg
When total fuel is less than 140 kg
items.explanation: Hovering in crosswinds or sideways flight with sustained roll angles greater than 15 deg is prohibited when fuel indication in either tank is less than 70 kg.

items.question: What is the maximum crossfeeding amount (tank with pump off, not supplying engines)?
items.explanation: Maximum crossfeeding amount is 228 kg.

items.question: What is the fuel pressure cautionary range?
items.explanation: Fuel pressure cautionary range is 0.0 to 0.5 bar.

items.question: What is the minimum fuel pressure for normal operation?
items.explanation: Minimum fuel pressure for normal operation is 0.6 bar.

items.question: What is the normal fuel pressure operation range?
items.explanation: Normal fuel pressure operation range is 0.6 to 2.1 bar.

items.question: What is the maximum fuel pressure?
items.explanation: Maximum fuel pressure is 2.1 bar.

items.question: What is the minimum engine oil pressure for normal operation?
items.explanation: Figure 1-27 shows minimum engine oil pressure for normal operation as 6.3 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: Engine Oil Pressure (Figure 1-27, p.1-55)

items.question: What is the maximum engine oil pressure for normal operation?
items.explanation: Figure 1-27 shows maximum engine oil pressure for normal operation as 8.9 bar.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: Engine Oil Pressure (Figure 1-27, p.1-55)

items.question: What is the minimum engine oil pressure allowed at ground idle (GI) for up to 1 minute?
items.explanation: Figure 1-27 specifies a minimum engine oil pressure at ground idle (GI) of 4.2 bar for up to 1 minute.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 1: Engine Oil Pressure (Figure 1-27, p.1-55)
